newsitem.title: USA: N.J. Treasurer says to join Prudential Insurance.
newsitem.headline: N.J. Treasurer says to join Prudential Insurance.

text.p: New Jersey Treasurer Brian Clymer, who helped balance a string of budgets while Gov. Christine Whitman cut income taxes 30 percent, said Wednesday he would resign to join the Prudential Insurance Co. of America.
Clymer announced his decision while testifying at a legislative budget committee hearing.
Clymer said he would join the insurance company in Newark as a vice president. The resignation will be effective sometime after the new budget takes effect on July 1.
After taking office in January 1994, Clymer was able to reduce state contributions to the state pension funds by restating certain actuarial assumptions.

This year he and Whitman proposed a $3.4 billion bond issue to eliminate most of the unfunded liability in the state's four pension funds, creating a $2 billion surplus that would enable the administration to forgo $647 million in contributions.
The proposal met resistance in the state Senate, and it has since been whittled down to $2.75 billion with a $590 million budget impact.
The fate of the proposal remains unclear in the legislature.

Clymer on Wednesday also told lawmakers he disagreed with a report by the Office of Legislative Services projecting that fiscal 1997 revenues would exceed expectations by $700 million. Clymer said his estimates put the year-end bonus at $450 million.

Whitman said the extra money would enable her to meet a new mandate from the state Supreme Court, which issued a ruling on Wednesday requiring that she spend another $248 million on the state's 28 poorest school districts.
Whitman also said the windfall would not eliminate the need for her pension bond plan.
